item.title: Cape Muroto and Tokushima's Wild Pacific Coast — Guide
item.description: South of Tokushima city, the prefecture’s coastline turns wild and elemental as it runs down the Pacific shore toward Cape Muroto, the great cape at the tip of the peninsula that divides Tokushima from Kochi’s Muroto. This is a coast of raw geology and open ocean: sheer rocky headlands, wave-cut platforms of uplifted seabed, crashing surf and vast horizons, quite different from the sheltered Seto Inland Sea in the north. The Muroto area is a UNESCO Global Geopark, its dramatic rock formations telling the story of land rising from the sea.

item.title: Irago Cape and the Atsumi Peninsula: Lighthouse at Land's End — Guide
item.description: Irago Cape marks the tip of the Atsumi Peninsula, the long green arm that encloses Mikawa Bay, and its white lighthouse — one of Japan’s fifty famous lighthouses — stands on the rocks where the bay’s calm waters meet the open Pacific swell. Beside it curves Koijigahama, the ‘Beach of the Road of Love’, a kilometre of pale sand celebrated in poetry and popular with couples, while the peninsula behind is one of Japan’s most productive flower and vegetable coasts, blanketed in yellow rapeseed blossom each early spring and serving some of Aichi’s best seafood in the port shacks around the ferry terminal.
